name: AuxPair.pairWeil_upsilon
summary: (k, k') acts on the datum by translating its residue function by k'^(-1) and multiplying by character values. At the places of Q the reduction of k'^(-1) is the parabolic j^(-1), which multiplies the incl-row determinant by det(j_00)^(-1), giving psi_w(det j_00)^(-1) at each w in Q, that is auxLevelChar(O)(j); at the places of M it is (diag(k, 1) j)^(-1), j fixing the incl-columns, which moves the inclusion matrix by k^(-1) (giving the factors psi(det k)^(-1)). Both kinds of places contribute inverse character values.

steps.claim: By pairWeil_modDatum_Kf, (k, k') acts on auxDatum(O) (a modDatum of resDetDatum with the vacuum at infinity) by translating the residue function x -> resDetDatum(k'^(-1) x k) and multiplying by character values.
steps.lean:
simp_rw [auxDatum, ← modDatum_vacVector, pairWeil_modDatum_Kf, modDatum_vacVector, ← map_inv _ k',
    ← _root_.smul_apply, ← map_smul]

steps.claim: Rewrite k'^(-1) through j^(-1) and reduce to an equality of residue functions at every matrix x.

Expand resDetDatum at the translated matrix: at the places of Q the reduction of k'^(-1) is j^(-1), which lies in the parabolic, so the incl-rows are multiplied by the incl-block of j^(-1) and their determinant by det(j_00)^(-1); this gives the factor psi_w(det j_00)^(-1) at each w in Q, the inverse character values that make up auxLevelChar(O)(j); the character values of the determinants are given by the tame part of the character (apply_det_eq_prod, rankTwist).
steps.lean:
simp [inv_apply_eq_inv', submatrix_mul_of_mem_rangeParabolic _ (inv_mem (j.2 (.inr _) ⟨⟩)),
    resDetDatum, firstBlockHom, -coe_units_inv, ↓reductionK₀_map_modulusResidue,
    submatrix_mul (e₂ := id), ↓Matrix.map_mul, by simpa [reduceFamily, funext_iff] using h,
    auxLevelChar, O.hasWeight.hasWeight_rankTwist.apply_det_eq_prod O.apart.1 O.tame_eq_one]

steps.claim: At the places of M, j fixes the incl-columns, so it leaves the inclusion matrix unchanged.
diag(k_w, 1) times the inclusion matrix is the inclusion matrix times k_w; cancel the invertible factor.
The remaining identity of products of character values (both sides vanish together when a determinant vanishes).
